title: Ice-Choked Harbor
premise: A master-and-apprentice relay at a northern ice-choked harbor. Captain Jiang Cheng and sailor Qingya guard the twin-tine ice hook; Qingya and Ashuang look nearly alike but wear different ear covers; after the Seal ice cutter is wrecked it must be avoided; the harbor ice log, count memory, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.
_comment: Author layer: humans only write entities + state machines + per-scene timelines (present + handwritten action + semantic events). op/gap/probe/forbidden are derived by complete_gt.py.

states.prime_icebreaker: A forty-year-old harbor icebreaking captain, frost clinging to his full beard, wearing a deep-blue oilskin coat and hobnail rubber boots, often shouldering a hemp-wrapped ice hook, gaze hard and steady.
states.frostbitten_cane: The same Jiang Cheng years later: right hand frostbitten and wrapped in thick felt, leaning on a wooden cane remade from an old oar, deep-blue oilskin coat rubbed white at the shoulder.
states.sea_burial_dead: Jiang Cheng has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the boathouse wooden bed, the old oilskin coat laid across his chest.

states.young_sailor: A sixteen-year-old sailor girl, blue cord wound around her braid tip, wearing a short oilskin vest, cheeks flushed red by sea wind, movements crisp.
states.adult_captain: A woman captain in her early twenties, still with blue cord on her braid tip, the oilskin vest now broad-shouldered, eyes steady, a small ice pick at her waist.

states.intact: A person-tall twin-tine ice hook, tines cold and bright steel, long shaft wrapped in non-slip hemp rope, harbor number carved at the shaft end.
states.tines_cracked: The same twin-tine ice hook with its outer tine burst by hard ice, hemp rope unraveled, white stress marks on the steel body.
states.tines_replaced: The twin-tine ice hook fitted with new tines and hemp rewound tight; new tines slightly brighter, harbor number at the shaft end still clear.

states.intact: An oilcloth-covered harbor ice log bound with waxed thread, inner pages charting tide lines, ice thickness, and berth numbers.
states.seawater_soaked: The same harbor ice log soaked through by seawater; oilcloth cover whitened and wrinkled, tide lines and ice-thickness figures bled into pale-blue blotches.

states.intact: A narrow ice cutter with a white seal painted on the bow, two rows of ice-blade fenders along the gunwales, thick hemp mooring line coiled at the stern.
states.wrecked: The Seal ice cutter crushed by pack ice; the bow seal split in two, ice-blade fenders torn off, only a shattered hull floating among broken ice.

states.young_rival: A youth whose face closely resembles Qingya's, but wearing snow-white plush earmuffs and a gray-blue oilskin vest, expression defiant.
states.remade_scarred: Remade Ashuang still wears snow-white earmuffs, a new ice-blade scar on his chin, gray-blue vest overlaid with a black cable strap.

E7.name: boathouse wheelhouse
E7.appearance: A wooden boathouse wheelhouse by the harbor; a tide board hangs by the stove, window glass skimmed with thin ice, mooring lines and spare ice hooks coiled on the wall.

E8.name: ice-choked harbor
E8.appearance: A northern winter harbor, surface crowded with broken ice, wooden-pile pier jutting over the ice sheet, distant icebreaker funnels breathing white mist.

E9.name: fish-shed dark corridor
E9.appearance: A damp cold dark corridor behind the fish shed, salted fish and buoys hanging on both sides, thin ice on the ground, yellowish light.

E10.name: abandoned foghorn tower
E10.appearance: An abandoned foghorn tower outside the harbor, white paint peeling, iron ladder rusted, low sea wind echoing in the tower cavity.

E11.name: Jiang brass plaque
E11.appearance: A brass harbor plaque nailed to the boathouse doorpost, engraved with 'Jiang Icebreaking' and a year, salt frost along the edges.

E12.name: ice-anchor heads
E12.appearance: Three spare iron ice-anchor heads, tips sharp, hanging from a short chain on the wheelhouse beam.

E13.name: blue-hull trawler
E13.appearance: A wide-body blue-hull trawler with no seal on the bow, deck piled with fishing nets, unlike the Seal ice cutter.

E14.name: harbor clerk Lao Kuai
E14.appearance: A lean harbor clerk also in a deep-blue oilskin coat, but with a silver-anchor port-authority badge on his cap, build close to Jiang Cheng's.

E15.name: pier signal lamps
E15.appearance: Five brass pier signal lamps hung in a row under the wheelhouse beam, red and green glass covers polished clear.

E16.name: fog horns
E16.appearance: Two black-iron fog horns fixed on the boathouse eaves, frosted mouths, low mournful blasts when fog rises.

E17.name: Haikui
E17.appearance: A tea-shed waitress girl at the pier, light-brown cord on her braid tip, at a glance resembling young Qingya, but wearing a red scarf with shy eyes.

E18.name: spare iron ice hook
E18.appearance: A half-person-tall spare iron ice hook, shape close to the twin-tine ice hook, but all black iron with no harbor number.

E19.name: repair pontoon
E19.appearance: A gray repair pontoon with rubber fenders along the edge, for docking shipwrights—never a narrow ice cutter.

features.E2: Qingya: blue cord on braid tip, short oilskin vest.
features.E6: Ashuang: face nearly identical to Qingya's, but snow-white earmuffs and gray-blue vest.

scenes.setting: Boathouse wheelhouse at dusk (signal lamps and fog horns)
actions: At dusk, Jiang Cheng slides open the frosted boathouse wheelhouse door and lays the twin-tine ice hook across beneath the tide board.

actions.action: Five brass pier signal lamps hang in a row under the wheelhouse beam; Jiang Cheng polishes each red and green glass cover.
Two black-iron fog horns are fixed on the boathouse eaves; Jiang Cheng pulls the test rope, sending a low blast through the thin mist.

actions: Jiang Cheng presses the twin tines of the ice hook into the ice-test trough, listening to the crisp bite of steel on blue ice.
He tightens the thick hemp mooring line by the wall and scores the night-tide mark on the tide board.
Jiang Cheng unties the waxed thread and opens the oilcloth-covered harbor ice log.
He pencils in inner-harbor ice thickness, outer-dike wind direction, and berths passable tonight.
Jiang Cheng closes the ice log and leans the twin-tine ice hook slantwise beside the cover so the sea wind cannot flip the pages.

scenes.setting: Harbor greets the apprentice (ice-anchor heads introduced)
actions: At the dawn ice-choked harbor, Jiang Cheng greets young Qingya steering the Seal ice cutter toward the wooden piles.

actions.action: Qingya leaps onto the pier and loops the Seal's stern thick hemp mooring line around a freezing wooden pile.
Jiang Cheng points to the three ice-anchor heads hanging from the short chain on the wheelhouse beam, teaching Qingya to read tip wear.
Qingya crouches at the Seal's bow, checking along the white seal painting whether the ice-blade fenders are loose.

actions: In the fish-shed dark corridor, Ashuang in snow-white earmuffs turns from the salted-fish shadows.
Ashuang brushes ice chips off his gray-blue vest, deliberately letting the earmuffs catch the light.
He hefts a coil of old mooring line and walks slowly away along the slick corridor.
Buoys sway at the corridor end; Ashuang's profile briefly mirrors in an iced puddle.
On the ice-choked harbor, Qingya and Ashuang brush past by the mooring-line pile—one with blue cord on her braid tip, one in snow-white earmuffs.
Qingya bends to tidy the Seal's cable knot while Ashuang watches her coldly across the ice.
Both turn at once toward the fog horn's low moan, then walk toward different piers.
Months later on a blizzard night, Jiang Cheng alone stands watch in the wheelhouse, twin-tine ice hook across his knees.

actions.action: He opens the harbor ice log and finds the oilcloth cover whitened by seawater soak; the tide-line figures have bled.

actions: Jiang Cheng spreads the wet pages by the stove and pencils back in the berth numbers still readable.
Through the long ice season, Jiang Cheng checks the tide board and wind flag in the wheelhouse every dawn.
Another snow night, he wraps his oilskin coat tight and listens to broken ice knock the boathouse piles.
At spring harbor opening, Jiang Cheng leans the ice hook by the door and watches the first string of fishing lamps return.
In midsummer with little ice, he unwraps the old hemp from the ice-hook shaft to dry.
In autumn fog, thin frost again films the wheelhouse window glass.
At daybreak Jiang Cheng patrols the ice-choked harbor; the Seal ice cutter rests at an inner-harbor berth.

actions.action: He bends to check the Seal's ice-blade fenders on both sides, confirming bolts have not been iced loose.
Jiang Cheng recoils loose pier mooring lines into neat rings and weights them with non-slip wooden wedges.
A wide-body blue-hull trawler steams in from the outer harbor, deck piled with nets, no seal on the bow.

actions: A blizzard presses the harbor flat; ice floes slam the wooden piles until they shudder.

actions.action: Jiang Cheng lunges to the wheelhouse door; the outer tine of the twin-tine ice hook bursts a white crack against hard ice.
The Seal ice cutter is driven toward the breakwater by a thick floe; the white seal on the bow twists violently.
Another wall of pack ice presses in; the Seal ice cutter's bow shatters, wrecked hull and fenders drifting into black water.
Jiang Cheng grips the cracked-tine ice hook and retreats into the wheelhouse, ice shards cutting a red line across his hand.

scenes.setting: Aftermath (ice cutter indirect mention · signal-lamp long range)

actions.action: The day after the blizzard, Jiang Cheng stands in the wheelhouse, looking down at the twin-tine ice hook with cracked tines.
On a blank page of the harbor ice log he writes the hour the Seal ice cutter was wrecked, the pencil tip nearly punching through the wet paper.
On the wheelhouse wall hangs the Seal ice cutter's snapped tiller; Jiang Cheng leaves it there a long time.
Jiang Cheng takes one of the five pier signal lamps from under the beam to light the bled tide lines in the ice log.
He wraps the Seal ice cutter's nameplate in oilcloth and tucks it into a wheelhouse wooden box.

scenes.setting: Tine replacement (spare ice hook false friend)
actions: Weeks later Jiang Cheng calls a pier blacksmith to the wheelhouse stove to remove the cracked tines.

actions.action: The smith first holds up a spare iron ice hook for comparison; similar shape, but no harbor number at the shaft end.
Once new tines are riveted into the steel body, the twin-tine ice hook is solid again and the hemp rewound tight.

actions: Jiang Cheng strikes the ice-test trough with the repaired ice hook and hears a clean crisp crack.

scenes.setting: False friends: pontoon and harbor clerk

actions.action: A gray repair pontoon is towed into the inner harbor for docking shipwrights—it is not the wrecked Seal ice cutter.
harbor clerk Lao Kuai leaps onto the wooden-pile pier and checks the tide board beside Jiang Cheng; both wear deep-blue oilskin coats.
Lao Kuai points at the repair pontoon to set tomorrow's de-icing route; Jiang Cheng only rests the repaired ice hook on his shoulder.

scenes.setting: False friend: Haikui who resembles Qingya

actions.action: A waitress named Haikui arrives at the pier tea shed; her light-brown braid cord swings in the wind, from afar like young Qingya.
Haikui tries tying a mooring knot; Jiang Cheng shakes his head, warning that her red scarf is too conspicuous—she is never Qingya.
At dusk years later, Jiang Cheng leans on the old-oar wooden cane and walks slowly to the abandoned foghorn tower door.
Those two black-iron fog horns still hang on the foghorn-tower eaves; wind pouring in makes a low echo.

actions: Jiang Cheng presses his thick-felt-wrapped right hand to the tower wall, as if bidding the old fairway farewell.

scenes.setting: Qingya returns · Jiang Cheng sea burial

actions.action: By day, adult Qingya steers a new icebreaker back outside the harbor and hurries toward the abandoned foghorn tower.

actions: Qingya reunites with cane-leaning Jiang Cheng under the tower door; they embrace through the sea wind.

actions.action: Beside the boathouse wooden bed, Qingya holds Jiang Cheng's thick-felt-wrapped hand and listens to distant tide on the shore.
Jiang Cheng's breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and is given to sea burial by old harbor custom.
Jiang Cheng's deep-blue old oilskin coat still hangs behind the boathouse door; Qingya smooths the rubbed-white shoulder.
Qingya stands before the Jiang brass plaque; Jiang Cheng's name is ringed in white by salt frost.
She traces with a fingertip the year Jiang Cheng left and renails the plaque tight on the doorpost.
Remade Ashuang walks in from outside the foghorn tower; the ice-blade scar on his chin pales in the cold light.

actions: Qingya and Ashuang stand side by side under the old tower doorway—one with blue braid cord, one in snow-white earmuffs.

actions.action: The shot returns to years ago—that sailor girl checking the seal painting at the bow appears again.

anchor.phrase: the sailor girl checking the seal painting at the bow

actions.action: The opening moment returns—in the wheelhouse, a twin-tine ice hook is pressed into the ice-test trough for the first time.

anchor.phrase: the twin-tine ice hook first pressed into the ice-test trough at the opening

actions.action: Flash to the fish-shed dark corridor—that lookalike figure in snow-white earmuffs slips past the salted-fish curtain.

anchor.phrase: the figure in snow-white earmuffs in the fish-shed dark corridor years ago

actions.action: Again those five small red-and-green glass lamps under the wheelhouse beam.

anchor.phrase: those five small red-and-green glass lamps under the wheelhouse beam

actions.action: Back to the iced inner harbor of first meeting—wooden piles, thin mist, and icebreaker funnels as before.

anchor.phrase: the iced inner harbor of first meeting

scenes.setting: Closing (ice-log long range · ice-anchor long range)

actions.action: Qingya opens that seawater-soaked harbor ice log and writes her first ice report on a new page.
The five pier signal lamps under the wheelhouse beam still glow; red and green light falls on her blue braid cord.
On the short chain at the beam side, those three ice-anchor heads still hang in neat order.
Qingya grips the tine-replaced twin-tine ice hook and pushes out toward the iced harbor.
